items.label: Park Systems Q2 FY2026 (08-14-2026)
items.signal_prefix: 2026 outlook in the half-year report: the company expects 2026 chip investme

set.signal: 2026 outlook in the half-year report: the company expects 2026 chip investment to keep centring on HBM, leading-edge logic and advanced packaging on AI server and data-center demand; it expects next-generation DRAM scaling and wider EUV adoption to raise demand for precision metrology and interest in its AFM solutions, and sees advanced packaging as a new growth opportunity. It plans to keep expanding R&D and cooperation with major chipmakers. The company expects the AFM market to grow fastest among microscopes, partly absorbing the SEM market, and believes it will grow faster than external forecasts.

items.reason: Third-party market-research data (MarketsandMarkets AFM market US$541.8M -> US$762.2M) is not captured (skill section 2); the company's own outlook is kept.

items.label: ISC IR presentation: KIND 18766 (06-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: AI test-socket roadmap in the IR Book 2026: memory sockets move from 0.2

set.signal: AI test-socket roadmap in the IR Book 2026: memory sockets move from 0.27mm ball pitch (2024) to 0.25mm (2025) and 0.23mm/0.2mm (2026), then to HBM/HBF, stacked LPDDR and FO-PLP sockets in 2027-2030; for AI computing and data-center advanced packages, the system-chip socket roadmap shows I/O counts rising from about 5,000 and 7,000 to about 15,000 and 25,000 across the NSP/TNSP, G3, WiDER, WiDER-Flex and WiDER+ families (2023 through 2026-2029) as package sizes grow from 70x50mm to over 130-150mm, with next-generation chiplet, FO-PLP and glass-substrate sockets from 2030. Portfolio phase 3 (in progress) extends from sockets into testers for AI, CPO, 3D packaging and HBM/HBF test.

items.reason: The slide's text layer does not tie ~7,000 I/O to NSP/TNSP in 2023 (it lists ~5,000 at 70x50mm and ~7,000 at 100x70mm across 2023-2024); rewritten without the unsupported pairing.
